title.zh: 卷一百十五 列傳第三 興宗孝康皇帝 睿宗興獻皇帝
title.en: Volume 115 Biographies 3: Emperor Xingzong Xiaokang, Emperor Ruizong Xingxian
title.raw: 卷一百十五 列傳第三 興宗孝康皇帝 睿宗興獻皇帝 Volume 115 Biographies 3: Emperor Xingzong Xiaokang, Emperor Ruizong Xingxian

sentences.zh: 興宗孝康皇帝 孝康皇后 呂太后 睿宗獻皇帝 獻皇后

translations.literal: Emperor Xingzong Xiaokang, Empress Xiaokang, Empress Dowager Lü, Emperor Ruizong Xingxian, and Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xingzong Xiaokang, Empress Xiaokang, Empress Dowager Lü, Emperor Ruizong Xingxian, and Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 興宗孝康皇帝標，太祖長子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xingzong Xiaokang, Biao, was the eldest son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Biao, posthumously honored as Emperor Xingzong Xiaokang, was Hongwu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 母高皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Gao.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Gao.

sentences.zh: 元至正十五年生於太平陳迪家。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng of Yuan he was born at Chen Di's house in Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in 1355 at the home of Chen Di in Taiping.

sentences.zh: 太祖為吳王，立為王世子，從宋濂受經。

translations.literal: When Taizu became Prince of Wu, [Biao] was installed as heir to the princely domain and studied the classics under Song Lian.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongwu was Prince of Wu, Biao was named heir to the principality and studied the classics under Song Lian.

sentences.zh: 吳元年，年十三矣，命省臨濠墓，諭曰：「商高宗舊勞于外，周成王早聞《無逸》之訓，皆知小民疾苦，故在位勤儉，為守成令主。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu, when he was thirteen, he was ordered to inspect the tombs at Linhao, and was instructed: "The Shang High Ancestor formerly toiled abroad; King Cheng of Zhou early heard the teachings of 'Against Idleness'—both knew the hardships of the common people, and therefore were diligent and frugal on the throne, becoming excellent rulers who preserved the inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu regime, when he was thirteen, he was sent to inspect the ancestral tombs at Fengyang. Hongwu instructed him: "The Shang High Ancestor once labored in the provinces; King Cheng of Zhou was taught the 'Against Idleness' early on—both understood the people's hardships, and so ruled diligently and frugally as successful heirs.

sentences.zh: 兒生長富貴，習于晏安。

translations.literal: You have grown up in wealth and honor, accustomed to ease and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: You have grown up amid wealth and ease.

sentences.zh: 今出旁近郡縣，遊覽山川，經歷田野，其因道途險易以知鞍馬勤勞，觀閭閻生業以知衣食艱難，察民情好惡以知風俗美惡，即祖宗所居，訪求父老，問吾起兵渡江時事，識之於心，以知吾創業不易。」

translations.literal: Now go out to the nearby commanderies and counties, tour mountains and rivers, pass through fields—thereby learn from the difficulty or ease of the roads the labor of saddle and horse, observe the livelihoods in lanes and hamlets to know the hardship of food and clothing, examine the people's likes and dislikes to know the beauty or ugliness of customs; at the places where the ancestors dwelt, seek out the elders, ask about the affairs when I raised troops and crossed the river, keep them in mind, to know that my founding the enterprise was not easy."
translations.idiomatic: Now travel through the neighboring prefectures and counties, see the land and its people, and learn from the roads what saddle-work costs, from village life what food and clothing require, and from local sentiment what customs are sound or corrupt. Where our forebears lived, question the elders about my crossing the Yangtze to raise the army, and fix it in your heart that founding this realm was no easy thing.

sentences.zh: 又命中書省擇官輔行。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Secretariat to select officials to accompany the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Secretariat to choose officials to accompany him on the tour.

sentences.zh: 凡所過郡邑城隍山川之神，皆祭以少牢。

translations.literal: At every commandery and county passed through, the spirits of city walls, moats, mountains, and rivers were all sacrificed to with the lesser tai-lao offering.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he passed, he offered the lesser tai-lao sacrifice to the local city-god, mountain, and river deities.

sentences.zh: 過太平訪迪家，賜白金五十兩。

translations.literal: Passing Taiping he visited Chen Di's house and bestowed fifty taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiping he visited Chen Di's home and gave him fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 至泗、濠告祭諸祖墓。

translations.literal: Arriving at Si and Hao, he announced sacrifices at the ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Sizhou and Fengyang and performed sacrifices at the ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 是冬從太祖觀郊壇，令左右導之農家，遍觀服食器具，又指道旁荊楚曰：「古用此為撲刑，以其能去風，雖傷不殺人。

translations.literal: That winter, following Taizu to observe the suburban altar, [Taizu] had attendants guide him to farm households to inspect food, clothing, and utensils in full, and again pointed to brambles by the road, saying: "In antiquity this was used for flogging punishment, because it can dispel wind; though it wounds, it does not kill.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, accompanying Hongwu to the suburban sacrifice, he was led through farmhouses to see how people ate and dressed. Hongwu pointed to brambles beside the road and said: "The ancients used these for the rod because they drive off wind: they hurt but do not kill.

sentences.zh: 古人用心仁厚如此，兒念之。」

translations.literal: The ancients' intent was so benevolent and generous—remember this, my son."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients' hearts were this humane—keep it in mind, my son.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年正月，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Hongwu, he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Hongwu's first year he was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帶刀舍人周宗上書乞教太子。

translations.literal: The sword-bearing attendant Zhou Zong submitted a memorial requesting instruction for the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zong, a sword-bearing attendant, memorialized asking that the crown prince receive formal instruction.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 中書省都督府請仿元制，以太子為中書令。

translations.literal: The Secretariat and the Commissioner's Office requested, following the Yuan system, to make the crown prince Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and the regional command asked to appoint the crown prince Secretariat Director, as under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 帝以元制不足法，令詹同考歷代東宮官制，選勳德老成及新進賢者，兼領東宮官。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the Yuan system was not worth taking as model, ordered Zhan Tong to examine the Eastern Palace offices of successive dynasties, and selected men of merit and long experience together with newly advanced worthies to hold Eastern Palace posts concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu rejected the Yuan precedent, had Zhan Tong study Eastern Palace institutions of past dynasties, and appointed both veteran meritorious officials and promising newcomers to dual posts in the heir apparent's establishment.

sentences.zh: 於是左丞相李善長兼太子少師，右丞相徐達兼太子少傅，中書平章錄軍國重事常遇春兼太子少保，右都督馮宗異兼右詹事，中書平章政事胡廷端、廖永忠、李伯升兼同知詹事院事，中書左、右丞趙庸、王溥兼副詹事，中書參政楊憲兼詹事丞，傅瓛兼詹事，同知大都督康茂才、張興祖兼左右率府使，大都督府副使顧時、孫興祖同知左右率府事，僉大都督府事吳楨、耿炳文兼左右率府副使，御史大夫鄧愈、湯和兼諭德，御史中丞劉基、章溢兼贊善大夫，治書侍御史文原吉、范顯祖兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Chancellor Li Shanchang concurrently served as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, Right Chancellor Xu Da as Junior Mentor, Secretariat Associate Director recording military and state affairs Chang Yuchun as Junior Guardian, Right Commissioner Feng Zongyi as Right Household Master, Secretariat Associate Directors Hu Tingduan, Liao Yongzhong, and Li Bosheng as Associate Directors of the Household Master's Office, Left and Right Secretariat Vice Directors Zhao Yong and Wang Pu as Deputy Household Masters, Secretariat Participating Secretary Yang Xian as Household Master Assistant, Fu Rong as Household Master, Associate Directors of the Great Capital Commission Kang Maocai and Zhang Xingzu as Left and Right Commandants of the Rate Offices, Deputy Commissioners of the Great Capital Commission Gu Shi and Sun Xingzu as Associate Commandants of the Rate Offices, Secretariat Affairs Commissioners Wu Zhen and Geng Bingwen as Deputy Commandants of the Rate Offices, Censor-in-Chief Deng Yu and Tang He as Preceptors, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Ji and Zhang Yi as Senior Companions in Goodness, and Investigating Secretaries Wen Yuanji and Fan Xianzu as Crown Prince Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shanchang, left chancellor, became junior tutor; Xu Da, right chancellor, junior mentor; Chang Yuchun, associate director for military affairs, junior guardian; Feng Zongyi, right commissioner, right household master; Hu Tingduan, Liao Yongzhong, and Li Bosheng, associate directors, associate household masters; Zhao Yong and Wang Pu, vice directors, deputy household masters; Yang Xian, participating secretary, household master assistant; Fu Rong, household master; Kang Maocai and Zhang Xingzu, associate capital commissioners, left and right rate-office commandants; Gu Shi and Sun Xingzu, deputy commissioners, associate commandants; Wu Zhen and Geng Bingwen, commissioners, deputy commandants; Deng Yu and Tang He, censors-in-chief, preceptors; Liu Ji and Zhang Yi, vice censors-in-chief, senior companions; Wen Yuanji and Fan Xianzu, investigating secretaries, crown prince's guests.

sentences.zh: 諭之曰：「朕於東宮不別設府僚，而以卿等兼領者，蓋軍旅未息，朕若有事於外，必太子監國。

translations.literal: He instructed them, saying: "I do not separately establish household staff for the Eastern Palace but have you hold posts concurrently because the army has not yet ceased; if I have business outside, the crown prince must oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: He told them: "I do not set up a separate Eastern Palace staff but make you serve concurrently because war is not over. If I must be away, the crown prince will govern.

sentences.zh: 若設府僚，卿等在內，事當啟聞，太子或聽斷不明，與卿等意見不合，卿等必謂府僚導之，嫌隙易生。

translations.literal: If household staff were set up, when you are inside and matters should be reported, the crown prince might judge unclearly and disagree with you; you would surely say the household staff guided him, and suspicion would easily arise.
translations.idiomatic: Separate palace staff would mean you inside reporting upward while the heir might decide poorly and clash with you—you would blame his tutors, and mistrust would follow.

sentences.zh: 又所以特置賓客諭德等官者，欲輔成太子德性，且選名儒為之，職此故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason for specially setting guests, preceptors, and the like is to assist in completing the crown prince's moral character, and to select renowned Confucians for the post—this is the purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Guests and preceptors exist to shape the heir's character; famous scholars were chosen for that reason.

sentences.zh: 昔周公教成王克詰戎兵，召公教康王張惶六師，此居安慮危，不忘武備。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou taught King Cheng to overcome military matters; the Duke of Shao taught King Kang to deploy the six armies in alarm—this is dwelling in peace yet considering danger, not forgetting military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou taught King Cheng to master arms; the Duke of Shao taught King Kang to keep the six hosts on alert—security that still remembers war.

sentences.zh: 蓋繼世之君，生長富貴，昵於安逸，不諳軍旅，一有緩急，罔知所措。

translations.literal: For heirs who succeed, growing up in wealth and honor, intimate with ease, unversed in military affairs—when urgency comes, they know not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Succession princes raised in luxury, unused to camps, are helpless when crisis strikes.

sentences.zh: 二公之言，其並識之。」

translations.literal: The words of the two dukes—both of you should keep them in mind together."
translations.idiomatic: Keep both dukes' lessons in mind.

sentences.zh: 是年，命選國子生國琦、王璞、張傑等十餘人，侍太子讀書禁中。

translations.literal: That year he ordered more than ten National University students such as Guo Qi, Wang Pu, and Zhang Jie selected to attend the crown prince reading in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year he chose more than ten National University students, including Guo Qi, Wang Pu, and Zhang Jie, to study with the crown prince inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 琦等入對謹身殿，儀狀明秀，應對詳雅。

translations.literal: When Qi and the others entered audience at the Hall of Cultivating the Person, their bearing was bright and elegant and their responses detailed and refined.
translations.idiomatic: When they were presented in the Hall of Cultivating the Person, they were graceful and answered with polish.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，因謂殿中侍御史郭淵友等曰：「諸生於文藝習矣，然與太子處，當端其心術，不流浮靡，庶儲德亦獲裨助。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and therefore said to the palace attendant Guo Yuanyou and others: "The students are practiced in literary arts, yet in dealing with the crown prince they should rectify their minds and not drift into frivolity, so that the heir's virtue may also receive assistance."
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu was pleased and told the attendant Guo Yuanyou and others: "These students know their letters, but with the heir they must steady their minds and avoid vanity, so his stored virtue may truly gain.

sentences.zh: 因厚賜之。

translations.literal: He therefore rewarded them generously.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave them rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以梁貞、王儀為太子賓客，秦庸、盧德明、張昌為太子諭德。

translations.literal: Before long, Liang Zhen and Wang Yi were made crown prince's guests, and Qin Yong, Lu Deming, and Zhang Chang crown prince's preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liang Zhen and Wang Yi became the crown prince's guests, and Qin Yong, Lu Deming, and Zhang Chang his preceptors.

sentences.zh: 先是，建大本堂，取古今圖籍充其中，征四方名儒教太子諸王，分番夜直，選才俊之士充伴讀。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Great Foundation Hall had been built, ancient and modern illustrated books filling it; famous Confucians from the four directions were summoned to teach the crown prince and princes, taking turns on night duty, and talented youths were chosen as study companions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Great Foundation Hall had been built and stocked with books; eminent scholars from across the realm taught the heir and the princes in rotating night watches, with gifted youths as companions.

sentences.zh: 帝時時賜宴賦詩，商搉古今，評論文字無虛日。

translations.literal: The emperor from time to time bestowed banquets and composed poetry, discussing ancient and modern matters and commenting on texts without a vacant day.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu often hosted them, composed verse, and debated texts and history day after day.

sentences.zh: 命諸儒作《鐘山龍蟠賦》。

translations.literal: He ordered the Confucians to compose "Ode on the Coiled Dragon of Bell Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: He had the scholars write "Ode on the Coiled Dragon of Bell Mountain."

sentences.zh: 置酒歡甚，自作《時雪賦》，賜東宮官。

translations.literal: Wine was set out and the joy was great; he himself composed "Ode on the Season's Snow" and bestowed it on Eastern Palace officials.
translations.idiomatic: At a lavish feast he himself wrote "Ode on the Season's Snow" and gave it to the Eastern Palace staff.

sentences.zh: 令三師、諭德朝賀東宮，東宮答拜。

translations.literal: He ordered the three mentors and preceptors to attend court congratulating the Eastern Palace, and the Eastern Palace to return the bow.
translations.idiomatic: He required the three mentors and preceptors to bow in court to the heir, who returned the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 又命東宮及王府官編緝古人行事可為鑒戒者，訓諭太子諸王。

translations.literal: He also ordered Eastern Palace and princely establishment officials to compile actions of the ancients that could serve as warnings, to instruct the crown prince and princes.
translations.idiomatic: He also had palace and princely staff compile exemplary and cautionary deeds of antiquity for the heir and the princes.

sentences.zh: 四年春，制《大本堂玉圖記》，賜太子。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he composed "Record of the Jade Diagram of the Great Foundation Hall" and bestowed it on the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourth year he wrote "Record of the Jade Diagram of the Great Foundation Hall" and gave it to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十年，令自今政事並啟太子處分，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he ordered that from then on all government affairs be first reported to the crown prince for disposition, and only afterward submitted [to the throne].
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he ruled that all routine business must first go to the crown prince for decision, then be reported upward.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「自古創業之君，曆涉勤勞，達人情，周物理，故處事鹹當。

translations.literal: He instructed, saying: "From antiquity, founding rulers have passed through toil, understood human feelings, and comprehended the patterns of things, and therefore handled affairs all appropriately.
translations.idiomatic: He told him: "Founding emperors know hardship, human nature, and how the world works, and so judge rightly.

sentences.zh: 守成之君，生長富貴，若非平昔練達，少有不謬者。

translations.literal: Rulers who preserve the inheritance, growing up in wealth and honor, unless practiced in ordinary times, seldom avoid error.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs raised in comfort, unless trained beforehand, almost always err.

sentences.zh: 故吾特命爾日臨群臣，聽斷諸司啟事，以練習國政。

translations.literal: Therefore I specially order you daily to face the ministers and hear and decide the reports of the various offices, to practice state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I order you daily to sit with ministers and decide their memorials—to practice government.

sentences.zh: 惟仁不失於疏暴，惟明不惑於邪佞，惟勤不溺於安逸，惟斷不牽于文法。

translations.literal: Only with benevolence will one not fail through lax violence; only with clarity will one not be deluded by wicked flattery; only with diligence will one not drown in ease; only with decisiveness will one not be dragged by legal formalities.
translations.idiomatic: Be benevolent and you will not slip into cruelty; be clear-sighted and flatterers will not deceive you; be diligent and ease will not drown you; be decisive and the code will not bind you.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆心為權度。

translations.literal: All these take the mind as the measure.
translations.idiomatic: In all of this the heart is the standard.

sentences.zh: 吾自有天下以來，未嘗暇逸，于諸事務惟恐毫髮失當，以負上天付託之意。

translations.literal: Since I possessed the empire I have never had leisure; in every affair I fear the slightest inappropriateness, lest I fail the trust Heaven bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the realm I have never rested; I fear the smallest misstep and failing Heaven's charge.

sentences.zh: 戴星而朝，夜分而寢，爾所親見。

translations.literal: Attending court by starlight, sleeping after midnight—you have seen this yourself.
translations.idiomatic: You have seen me at court before dawn and abed only after midnight.

sentences.zh: 爾能體而行之，天下之福也。」

translations.literal: If you can embody and carry this out, it will be the empire's good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: If you can live by this, the realm will be fortunate.

sentences.zh: 時令儒臣為太子講《大學衍義》。

translations.literal: At the time Confucian officials were ordered to lecture the crown prince on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian officials were then assigned to lecture him on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，置詹事院。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Household Master's Office was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the Household Master's Office was set up.

sentences.zh: 二十四年八月，敕太子巡撫陝西。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year an edict ordered the crown prince to tour and pacify Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year Hongwu ordered the crown prince to inspect Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝以應天、開封為南北京，臨濠為中都。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had taken Yingtian and Kaifeng as the southern and northern capitals and Linhao as the central capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hongwu had named Nanjing and Kaifeng the southern and northern capitals and Fengyang the central capital.

sentences.zh: 御史鬍子祺上書曰：「天下形勝地可都者四。

translations.literal: The censor Hu Ziqi submitted a memorial, saying: "In the empire there are four strategically superior places that may serve as capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Ziqi wrote: "Four places in the realm are fit to be capitals.

sentences.zh: 河東地勢高，控制西北，堯嘗都之，然其地苦寒。

translations.literal: The land east of the [Yellow] River is high in terrain and controls the northwest; Yao once made it his capital, yet the region is bitterly cold.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanxi plateau commands the northwest and Yao once ruled there, but it is bitterly cold.

sentences.zh: 汴梁襟帶河、淮，宋嘗都之，然其地平曠，無險可憑。

translations.literal: Bianliang is girded by the Yellow and Huai rivers; Song once made it capital, yet its land is broad and level, with no terrain to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Bianliang lies between the Yellow and Huai; the Song capitalized there, but the plain offers no natural defense.

sentences.zh: 洛陽周公卜之，周、漢遷之，然嵩、邙非有殽函、終南之阻，澗、瀍、伊、洛非有涇、渭、灞、滻之雄。

translations.literal: Luoyang the Duke of Zhou divined for; Zhou and Han moved there, yet Song and Mang lack the barriers of Xiao-Han and Zhongnan, and the Jian, Chan, Yi, and Luo lack the might of the Jing, Wei, Ba, and Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang was divined by the Duke of Zhou and used by Zhou and Han, yet Mount Song and Mangshan are not Xiao-Han or Zhongnan, nor are the Jian, Chan, Yi, and Luo the Jing, Wei, Ba, and Chan.

sentences.zh: 夫據百二河山之勝，可以聳諸侯之望，舉天下莫關中若也。」

translations.literal: To hold the superiority of the hundred-and-two rivers and mountains can make the feudal lords look up; in all the empire none matches Guanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: Who holds the hundred-and-two defiles of Guanzhong commands every lord's gaze; nowhere else in the realm compares.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu commended the memorial.

sentences.zh: 至是，諭太子曰：「天下山川惟秦地號為險固，汝往以省觀風俗，慰勞秦父老子弟。」

translations.literal: At this time he instructed the crown prince, saying: "Among the mountains and rivers of the empire, only Qin territory is called strategically secure; go to observe customs and comfort the elders and people of Qin."
translations.idiomatic: He now told the heir: "Of all landscapes only Qin is called impregnable; go observe its customs and comfort its elders.

sentences.zh: 於是擇文武諸臣扈太子行。

translations.literal: Thereupon civil and military officials were chosen to escort the crown prince on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were then chosen to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 既行，使諭曰：「爾昨渡江，震雷忽起于東南，導爾前行，是威震之兆也。

translations.literal: After he had set out, a messenger instructed, saying: "Yesterday when you crossed the river, thunder suddenly rose in the southeast and guided you forward—this is an omen of awe-inspiring might.
translations.idiomatic: After his departure a message said: "When you crossed the river yesterday, thunder rose in the southeast and led you on—a sign of commanding majesty.

sentences.zh: 然一旬久陰不雨，佔有陰謀，宜慎舉動，嚴宿衛，施仁布惠，以回天意。」

translations.literal: Yet for ten days clouds have long been overcast without rain; the divination indicates hidden plotting; you should be cautious in action, strict in night guards, and extend benevolence and spread favor to turn Heaven's mind."
translations.idiomatic: Yet ten days of cloud without rain suggest conspiracy; move carefully, guard the camp strictly, and show mercy and grace to move Heaven.

sentences.zh: 仍申諭從行諸臣以宿頓聞。

translations.literal: He again instructed the accompanying officials to report on lodging and halts.
translations.idiomatic: He again told the escort to report each night's halt.

sentences.zh: 比還，獻陝西地圖，遂病。

translations.literal: When he returned he presented a map of Shaanxi, and then fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he presented a map of Shaanxi, then fell ill.

sentences.zh: 病中上言經略建都事。

translations.literal: While ill he submitted a memorial on strategy for establishing the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From his sickbed he memorialized on capital strategy.

sentences.zh: 明年四月丙子薨，帝慟哭。

translations.literal: The next year, on the bingzi day of the fourth month, he died; the emperor wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on the bingzi day of the fourth month, he died; Hongwu wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 禮官議期喪，請以日易。

translations.literal: The ritual officials discussed the mourning period and requested to substitute days for months.
translations.idiomatic: The ritualists proposed shortening the mourning period by counting days for months.

sentences.zh: 及當除服，帝不忍。

translations.literal: When the time came to end mourning, the emperor could not bear to.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning should have ended, Hongwu could not bring himself to do it.

sentences.zh: 禮官請之，始釋服視朝。

translations.literal: The ritual officials pressed the request, and only then did he remove mourning and attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Only after they pressed him did he leave mourning and hold court.

sentences.zh: 八月庚申祔葬孝陵東，諡曰懿文。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the eighth month he was buried in association east of the Xiaoling tomb, with posthumous title Yiwen.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the eighth month he was buried beside Xiaoling, with the posthumous title Yiwen.

sentences.zh: 睿宗興獻皇帝祐杬，憲宗第四子。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong Xingxian, Youyuan, was the fourth son of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youyuan, posthumously Emperor Ruizong Xingxian, was the fourth son of the Chenghua emperor.

sentences.zh: 母邵貴妃。

translations.literal: His mother was the Honored Consort Shao.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Honored Consort Shao.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年封興王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua he was enfeoffed Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 23 he was enfeoffed Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年建邸德安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi his residence was established at De'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4 his princely mansion was built at De'an.

sentences.zh: 已，改安陸。

translations.literal: Later it was changed to Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: It was later moved to Anlu.

sentences.zh: 七年之籓，舟次龍江，有慈烏數萬繞舟，至黃州復然，人以為瑞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, going to his fief, when the boat moored at Longjiang, tens of thousands of benevolent crows circled the vessel; at Huangzhou it happened again, and people took it as an auspice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, en route to his fief, his boat at Longjiang was circled by tens of thousands of crows; the same occurred at Huangzhou, and people called it a portent.

sentences.zh: 謝疏陳五事。

translations.literal: In his memorial of thanks he set forth five matters.
translations.idiomatic: In his thanksgiving memorial he laid out five points.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘉之，賜予異諸弟。

translations.literal: Xiaozong praised it and bestowed gifts different from those given his other brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongzhi emperor praised him and gave gifts beyond those for his brothers.

sentences.zh: 王薨二年而武宗崩，召王世子入嗣大統，是為世宗。

translations.literal: Two years after the prince's death Wuzong died; the prince's heir was summoned to succeed the great succession—this is Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after the prince's death the Wuzong emperor died; the prince's son was summoned to the throne as the Jiajing emperor.

sentences.zh: 禮臣毛澄等援漢定陶、宋濮王故事，考孝宗，改稱王為「皇叔父興獻大王」，王妃為「皇叔母」。

translations.literal: The ritual officials Mao Cheng and others cited the precedents of Dingtao in Han and Prince Pu of Song, took Xiaozong as the object of sacrifice, and changed the prince's title to "Imperial Uncle Father, Great King of Xingxian," and the princess to "Imperial Aunt Mother."
translations.idiomatic: Ritualists led by Mao Cheng cited Han Dingtao and Song Prince Pu, made Xiaozong the sacrificial father, and styled the prince "Imperial Uncle Father, Great King of Xingxian" and his consort "Imperial Aunt Mother."

sentences.zh: 帝命廷臣集議，未決。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered court officials to assemble for discussion; no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing ordered a court debate; no conclusion was reached.

sentences.zh: 進士張璁上書請考興獻王，帝大悅。

translations.literal: The presented scholar Zhang Cong submitted a memorial requesting sacrifice to Prince Xingxian; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Presented scholar Zhang Cong memorialized to worship Prince Xingxian; Jiajing was delighted.

sentences.zh: 會母妃至自安陸，止通州不入。

translations.literal: When the prince's mother arrived from Anlu she stopped at Tongzhou and did not enter [the capital].
translations.idiomatic: When his mother came from Anlu she halted at Tongzhou and would not enter the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝啟張太后，欲避天子位，奉母妃歸籓。

translations.literal: The emperor informed Empress Dowager Zhang, wishing to yield the Son of Heaven's position and return with his mother to the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing told Empress Dowager Zhang he would abdicate and return with his mother to Anlu.

sentences.zh: 群臣惶懼。

translations.literal: The ministers were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were terrified.

sentences.zh: 太后命進王為興獻帝，妃為興獻後。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered the prince advanced to Emperor Xingxian and the consort to Empress Xingxian.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager promoted the prince to Emperor Xingxian and his consort to Empress Xingxian.

sentences.zh: 璁更為《大禮或問》以進，而主事霍韜、桂萼，給事中熊浹議與璁合。

translations.literal: Cong further composed "Questions on the Great Rites" and presented it; Section Director Huo Tao and Gui E, and Supervising Secretary Xiong Shi, argued in agreement with Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong also wrote "Questions on the Great Rites"; Huo Tao and Gui E, section directors, and Xiong Shi, supervising secretary, agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 帝因諭輔臣楊廷和、蔣冕、毛紀，帝、後加稱「皇」。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon instructed the chief ministers Yang Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji to add the title "Imperial" to emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing then told chief ministers Yang Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji to add "Imperial" to the new titles.

sentences.zh: 廷和等合廷臣爭之，未決。

translations.literal: Tinghe and the others joined court officials in disputing it; still no decision.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tinghe and others united the court in opposition; the matter remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，禁中火，廷和及給事中鄧繼曾、硃鳴陽引五行五事，為廢禮之證。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, fire broke out in the Forbidden City; Tinghe and Supervising Secretaries Deng Jiceng and Zhu Mingyang cited the Five Elements and Five Affairs as proof for abolishing the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 a fire struck the Forbidden City; Yang Tinghe and supervising secretaries Deng Jiceng and Zhu Mingyang invoked the Five Elements and Five Affairs as omens against the new rites.

sentences.zh: 乃輟稱「皇」，加稱本生父興獻帝，尊園曰陵，黃屋監衛如制，設祠署安陸，歲時享祀，用十二籩豆，樂用八佾。

translations.literal: Thereupon they ceased the title "Imperial," added the title Biological Father Emperor Xingxian, honored the garden as a mausoleum, yellow-canopied guard and escort as prescribed, established a sacrificial office at Anlu with seasonal offerings, using twelve trays of offerings and music with eight rows of dancers.
translations.idiomatic: The court dropped "Imperial," styled his biological father Emperor Xingxian, made the garden a mausoleum with imperial guard, set up a shrine at Anlu with seasonal rites, twelve offering trays, and eight rows of dancers.

sentences.zh: 帝心終未慊。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart was still not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing was still not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 三年加稱為本生皇考恭穆獻皇帝，興國太后為本生聖母章聖皇太后，建廟奉先殿西，曰觀德殿，祭如太廟。

translations.literal: In the third year they added the titles Biological Imperial Father, Respectful and Solemn Emperor Xingxian, and Biological Holy Mother, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng; a temple was built west of the Hall of Ancestors, called the Hall of Observing Virtue, with sacrifices like the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he added "Biological Imperial Father, Respectful and Solemn Emperor Xingxian" and "Biological Holy Mother, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng," and built the Hall of Observing Virtue west of the Ancestral Hall with Grand Temple rites.

sentences.zh: 七月，諭去本生號。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he instructed that the biological titles be removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he ordered the word "biological" dropped.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔稱孝宗皇伯考，稱獻皇帝曰皇考。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict styled Xiaozong Imperial Uncle-Grandfather and the Xingxian emperor Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict called Xiaozong "Imperial Uncle-Grandfather" and the Xingxian emperor "Imperial Father."

sentences.zh: 璁、萼等既驟貴，幹進者爭以言禮希上意。

translations.literal: After Cong, E, and the others had suddenly risen in rank, those who sought advancement vied to speak on ritual to please the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Cong and Gui E were suddenly elevated, careerists competed to opine on ritual to please Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 百戶隨全、錄事錢子勳言獻皇帝宜遷葬天壽山。

translations.literal: Company Commander Sui Quan and Clerk Qian Zixun said the Xingxian emperor should be reburied at Tianshou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Company commander Sui Quan and clerk Qian Zixun said the Xingxian emperor should be moved to Tianshou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書席書議：「高皇帝不遷祖陵，太宗不遷孝陵，蓋其慎也。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xi Shu argued: "The High Emperor did not move the ancestral tomb; Taizong did not move the Xiaoling tomb—such is their caution.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Xi Shu argued: "Taizu did not relocate the ancestral mound, nor Taizong Xiaoling—such was their caution.

sentences.zh: 小臣妄議山陵，宜罪。」

translations.literal: Petty officials rashly discuss the imperial tomb—they should be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Petty officials who rashly discuss the imperial tomb should be punished.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書趙璜亦言不可。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhao Huang also said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhao Huang also said it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尊陵名曰顯陵。

translations.literal: The honored mausoleum was named Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tomb was given the name Xianling.

sentences.zh: 明年，修《獻皇帝實錄》，建世廟于太廟左。

translations.literal: The next year they compiled the Veritable Records of the Xian Emperor and built the World Temple to the left of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the court compiled the Veritable Records of the Xingxian emperor and built the World Temple east of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 六年，以觀德殿狹隘，改建崇先殿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because the Hall of Observing Virtue was cramped, they rebuilt it as the Hall of Honoring the Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the cramped Hall of Observing Virtue was rebuilt as the Hall of Honoring the Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 七年，命璁等集《明倫大典》，成，加上尊諡曰恭睿淵仁寬穆純聖獻皇帝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he ordered Cong and others to compile the Great Canon of Ming Moral Relations; when it was finished, an elevated posthumous title was added: Respectful, Sagacious, Profound, Benevolent, Broad, Solemn, Pure, and Holy Xian Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Zhang Cong and others compiled the Great Canon of Ming Moral Relations; on completion the emperor received the extended posthumous title Respectful, Sagacious, Profound, Benevolent, Broad, Solemn, Pure, and Holy Xian Emperor.

sentences.zh: 親製《顯陵碑》，封松林山為純德山，從祀方澤，次五鎮，改安陸州為承天府。

translations.literal: He personally composed the "Stele of Xianling," enfeoffed Pine Grove Mountain as Mount Chunde, added it to the sacrifices at the Earth Altar ranking below the Five Marchmounts, and changed Anlu Prefecture to Chengtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Stele of Xianling himself, renamed Pine Grove Mountain Mount Chunde, ranked it in the earth-altar sacrifices below the Five Marchmounts, and elevated Anlu to Chengtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十七年，通州同知豐坊請加尊皇考廟號，稱宗以配上帝。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Tongzhou Assistant Prefect Feng Fang requested adding an honored temple name for the imperial father, styling him as a lineage founder to match the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Assistant Prefect Feng Fang of Tongzhou asked that the emperor's father receive a temple name as "founder" to share heaven's altar.

sentences.zh: 九月，加上尊諡知天守道洪德淵仁寬穆純聖恭儉敬文獻皇帝，廟號睿宗，祔太廟，位次武宗上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an elevated posthumous title was added: Knowing Heaven, Upholding the Way, Vast Virtue, Profound Benevolence, Broad Solemnity, Pure Holiness, Respectful Frugality, and Cultivated Culture Xian Emperor; temple name Ruizong; enshrined in the Grand Temple, ranked above Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he received the full posthumous title Knowing Heaven, Upholding the Way, Vast Virtue, Profound Benevolence, Broad Solemnity, Pure Holiness, Respectful Frugality, and Cultivated Culture Xian Emperor, temple name Ruizong, enshrined in the Grand Temple above Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 明堂大享，奉主配天，罷世廟之祭。

translations.literal: At the Bright Hall great offering, the tablet was presented to match Heaven, and the World Temple sacrifices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall he was paired with Heaven in the great sacrifice, and worship at the World Temple ceased.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，芝生世廟柱，復作玉芝官祀焉。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, fungus grew on a pillar of the World Temple, and the Jade-Fungus Shrine was built again for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year lingzhi fungus appeared on a World Temple pillar, and the Jade-Fungus Shrine was restored.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，乃罷明堂配享。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, the Bright Hall matching sacrifice was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Muzong emperor the Bright Hall pairing rite was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，楊廷和等議封益王次子崇仁王厚炫為興王，奉獻帝祀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Tinghe and others had proposed enfeoffing the second son of Prince Yi, Prince Chongren Hou Xuan, as Prince of Xing to maintain sacrifices to the Xian Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Tinghe had proposed making Prince Yi's second son, Chongren prince Hou Xuan, Prince of Xing to tend the Xian emperor's cult.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: It was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 興國封除。

translations.literal: The enfeoffment of Xing was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Xing principality was abolished.

sentences.zh: 獻帝有長子厚熙，生五日而殤。

translations.literal: The Xian Emperor had an eldest son, Houxi, who died on the fifth day after birth.
translations.idiomatic: The Xian emperor's eldest son Houxi died five days after birth.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年贈岳王，諡曰懷獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yue, with posthumous title Huai Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 4 he was posthumously made Prince of Yue with the title Huai Xian.

sentences.zh: 皇后蔣氏，世宗母也。

translations.literal: Empress Jiang was Shizong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jiang was the Jiajing emperor's mother.

sentences.zh: 父斅，大興人，追封玉田伯。

translations.literal: Her father Jiao was a native of Daxing; posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jiao came from Daxing and was posthumously made Earl of Yutian.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年冊為興王妃。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi she was installed as Princess of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 5 she was invested as Princess of Xing.

sentences.zh: 世宗入承大統，即位三日，遣使詣安陸奉迎，而令廷臣議推尊禮。

translations.literal: When Shizong entered to succeed the great succession, three days after his accession he dispatched envoys to Anlu to welcome her, and ordered court officials to discuss rites of exaltation.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after Jiajing succeeded the throne he sent envoys to Anlu to fetch her and ordered the court to debate her honors.

sentences.zh: 咸謂宜考孝宗，而稱興王為皇叔父，妃為皇叔母。

translations.literal: All said it was fitting to take Xiaozong as the object of sacrifice, and to style the Prince of Xing as Imperial Uncle Father and the consort as Imperial Aunt Mother.
translations.idiomatic: Officials agreed he should worship Xiaozong and call the Xing prince "Imperial Uncle Father" and his consort "Imperial Aunt Mother."

sentences.zh: 議三上，未決。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted three times without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Three memorials brought no decision.

sentences.zh: 會妃將至，禮臣上入宮儀，由崇文門入東安門，皇帝迎于東華門。

translations.literal: When the consort was about to arrive, the ritual officials presented the palace-entry protocol: enter by Chongwen Gate and Dong'an Gate, with the emperor welcoming at Donghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: As she approached, ritualists proposed entry through Chongwen and Dong'an gates with the emperor greeting her at Donghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing refused.

sentences.zh: 再議由正陽門入大明、承天、端門，從王門入宮。

translations.literal: They debated again entering by Zhengyang Gate through Daming, Chengtian, and Duanyang gates, and entering the palace by the Prince's Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A second plan had her enter by Zhengyang Gate through Daming, Chengtian, and Duanyang, then by the Prince's Gate.

sentences.zh: 又不許。

translations.literal: Again it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: That too was refused.

sentences.zh: 王門，諸王所出入門也。

translations.literal: The Prince's Gate was the gate through which princes entered and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince's Gate was reserved for princes.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「聖母至，御太后車服，從御道入，朝太廟。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "When the Holy Mother arrives, she shall use the empress dowager's carriage and robes, enter by the imperial roadway, and attend the Grand Temple."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "When the Holy Mother arrives she shall wear empress-dowager regalia, take the imperial roadway, and worship at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 故事：後妃無謁廟禮。

translations.literal: Precedent: consorts had no rite of attending the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent held that consorts did not worship at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 禮臣難之。

translations.literal: The ritual officials objected.
translations.idiomatic: The ritualists objected.

sentences.zh: 時妃至通州，聞考孝宗，恚曰：「安得以吾子為他人子！」

translations.literal: At the time the consort had reached Tongzhou; hearing that Xiaozong was to be taken as the object of sacrifice, she angrily said: "How can my son be made another man's son!"
translations.idiomatic: At Tongzhou she learned Xiaozong would be his ritual father and raged: "How can my son be treated as another man's child!

sentences.zh: 留不進。

translations.literal: She stayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: She halted and would not enter the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝涕泣願避位。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and wished to yield the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing wept and offered to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 群臣以慈壽太后命，改稱興獻後，乃入。

translations.literal: The ministers, by order of Empress Dowager Cishou, changed her title to Empress Xingxian, and only then did she enter.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Dowager Cishou's command ministers styled her Empress Xingxian, after which she entered.

sentences.zh: 以太后儀謁奉先、奉慈二殿，不廟見。

translations.literal: With empress dowager rites she paid respects at the Halls of Venerating the Ancestors and Cherishing the Kind, but did not perform the temple audience.
translations.idiomatic: She worshipped at the Halls of Venerating the Ancestors and Cherishing the Kind in dowager rites but did not perform the full temple audience.

sentences.zh: 元年改稱興國太后。

translations.literal: In the first year her title was changed to Empress Dowager of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 she was titled Empress Dowager of Xing.

sentences.zh: 三年乃上尊號曰本生章聖皇太后。

translations.literal: Only in the third year was the elevated title Biological Holy Mother, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year she received the title Biological Holy Mother, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，用張璁等言，尊為聖母章聖皇太后。

translations.literal: That autumn, following Zhang Cong and others' advice, she was honored as Holy Mother, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, on Zhang Cong's advice, she was honored as Holy Mother, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng.

sentences.zh: 五年，獻帝世廟成，奉太后入謁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the Xian Emperor's World Temple was completed, the empress dowager was led in to worship.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the Xian emperor's World Temple was finished, she was led in to worship.

sentences.zh: 七年，上尊號曰慈仁。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the elevated title Ciren was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the honorific Ciren was added.

sentences.zh: 九年，頒太后所制《女訓》於天下。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the empress dowager's self-composed Admonitions for Women was promulgated throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year her Admonitions for Women was issued empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 十五年，奉太后謁天壽山陵，命諸臣進賀行殿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, leading the empress dowager to worship at the Tianshou Mountain tomb, he ordered the ministers to present congratulations at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he took her to worship at Tianshou Mountain and ordered ministers to offer congratulations at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 是年加上尊號曰康靜貞壽。

translations.literal: That year the elevated title Tranquil, Chaste, and Long-lived was added.
translations.idiomatic: That year the honorific Tranquil, Chaste, and Long-lived was added.

sentences.zh: 十七年十二月崩，諭禮、工二部將改葬獻皇帝于大峪山，以駙馬都尉京山侯崔元為奉迎行禮使，兵部尚書張瓚為禮儀護行使，指揮趙俊為吉凶儀仗官，翊國公郭勳知聖母山陵事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year she died; he instructed the Ministries of Rites and Works to reinter the Xian Emperor at Dayu Mountain, appointing Commandant-in-Chief of the Capital Guards and Jingshan Marquis Cui Yuan as envoy for welcoming and performing rites, Minister of War Zhang Zan as envoy for protecting ritual, Commander Zhao Jun as officer of auspicious and inauspicious regalia, and Defender of the State Duke Guo Xun to oversee the Holy Mother's tomb affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year she died. Jiajing ordered the Ministries of Rites and Works to move the Xian emperor to Dayu Mountain, naming Cui Yuan, commandant and Jingshan marquis, welcoming envoy; Zhang Zan, minister of war, ritual escort; Zhao Jun, commander, regalia officer; and Guo Xun, defender of the state, to manage the dowager's tomb.

sentences.zh: 已，帝親幸大峪相視，令議奉太后南詣合葬。

translations.literal: Later the emperor personally visited Dayu to inspect it and ordered discussion of bringing the empress dowager south for joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: He then inspected Dayu in person and ordered plans to bring the dowager south for joint burial.

sentences.zh: 而禮部尚書嚴嵩等言：「靈駕北來，慈宮南詣，共一舉耳。

translations.literal: But Minister of Rites Yan Song and others said: "The imperial coffin comes north and the Kind Palace goes south—it is a single undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yan Song argued: "The imperial coffin travels north while the Kind Palace goes south—one journey serves both.

sentences.zh: 大峪可朝發夕至，顯陵遠在承天，恐陛下春秋念之。

translations.literal: Dayu can be reached setting out in the morning and arriving by evening; Xianling is far away at Chengtian—we fear Your Majesty, in the autumn of life, will brood on it.
translations.idiomatic: Dayu lies a day's march away, but Xianling is distant at Chengtian; we fear Your Majesty's advancing years will be burdened by the distance.

sentences.zh: 臣謂如初議便。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the original proposal is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant thinks the first plan is better.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「成祖豈不思皇祖耶，何以南孝陵？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Did Chengzu not think of his imperial grandfather—why then the southern Xiaoling?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing replied: "Did the Yongle emperor not honor his grandfather—why keep Xiaoling in the south?"

sentences.zh: 因止崔元等毋行，而令趙俊往，且啟視幽宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped Cui Yuan and the others from going, but ordered Zhao Jun to proceed and also to open and inspect the underground palace.
translations.idiomatic: He halted Cui Yuan's mission but sent Zhao Jun to open and inspect the underground palace.

sentences.zh: 是年上尊諡曰慈孝貞順仁敬誠一安天誕聖獻皇后。

translations.literal: That year the posthumous title Kind, Filial, Chaste, Obedient, Benevolent, Respectful, Sincere, Unified, Heaven-Bestowing, Sagely Xian Empress was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: That year she received the posthumous title Kind, Filial, Chaste, Obedient, Benevolent, Respectful, Sincere, Unified, Heaven-Bestowing, Sagely Xian Empress.

sentences.zh: 明年，俊歸，謂顯陵不吉，遂議南巡。

translations.literal: The next year Jun returned, saying Xianling was inauspicious, and thereupon they debated a southern tour.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhao Jun returned reporting Xianling inauspicious, and a southern tour was proposed.

sentences.zh: 九卿大臣許贊等諫。

translations.literal: The nine ministers and great officials Xu Zan and others remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Nine ministers led by Xu Zan remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing ignored them.

sentences.zh: 左都御史王廷相又諫。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang remonstrated again.
translations.idiomatic: Left censor-in-chief Wang Tingxiang remonstrated again.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕豈空行哉，為吾母耳！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Would I travel for nothing? It is for my mother!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing said: "Do you think I travel for sport? This is for my mother!

sentences.zh: 已而侍御呂柟、給事中曾烶、御史劉賢、郎中岳倫等復相繼疏諫。

translations.literal: Before long the attendant Lü Zhen, Supervising Secretary Zeng Yan, Censor Liu Xian, Section Director Yue Lun, and others again submitted memorials in succession remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Lü Zhen, supervising secretary Zeng Yan, censor Liu Xian, section director Yue Lun, and others then memorialized in turn.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He still would not listen.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝至承天，謁顯陵，作新宮焉，曰：「待合葬也。」

translations.literal: In the third month the emperor reached Chengtian, worshipped at Xianling, and built a new palace, saying: "Awaiting joint burial."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he reached Chengtian, worshipped at Xianling, and built a new palace "to await joint burial.

sentences.zh: 歸過慶都，御史謝少南言：「慶都有堯母墓，佚於祀典，請祀之。」

translations.literal: On the return, passing Qingdu, Censor Xie Shaonan said: "Qingdu has the tomb of Yao's mother, omitted from the sacrificial canon—please sacrifice to it."
translations.idiomatic: Returning through Qingdu, censor Xie Shaonan noted Yao's mother's tomb there, absent from the canon of sacrifices, and asked that it be enshrined.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「帝堯父母異陵，可知合葬非古。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Emperor Yao's parents lie in separate tombs—this shows joint burial is not ancient."
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing replied: "Emperor Yao's parents lie in separate tombs—joint burial is not ancient practice."

sentences.zh: 即拜少南左春坊左司直兼翰林院檢討，定議葬大峪山。

translations.literal: He immediately promoted Shaonan to Left Director of the Eastern Palace Left Secretariat and Concurrent Hanlin Academician Examiner, and fixed the decision to bury at Dayu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately promoted Xie Shaonan to left director of the Eastern Palace and Hanlin examiner, fixing burial at Dayu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 四月，帝謁長陵，諭嚴嵩曰：「大峪不如純德。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month the emperor worshipped at Changling and instructed Yan Song, saying: "Dayu is not as good as Chunde."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, visiting Changling, he told Yan Song: "Dayu is inferior to Chunde.

sentences.zh: 仍命崔元護梓宮南祔。

translations.literal: He still ordered Cui Yuan to escort the coffin south for association.
translations.idiomatic: He still ordered Cui Yuan to escort the coffin south for association.

sentences.zh: 閏七月，合葬顯陵，主祔睿宗廟。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month they were jointly buried at Xianling, and her tablet was associated in the Ruizong temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month she was buried with him at Xianling and her spirit tablet joined the Ruizong temple.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：興宗、睿宗雖未嘗身為天子，而尊號徽稱典禮具備，其實有不容泯者。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Although Xingzong and Ruizong never personally became Sons of Heaven, their honored titles, fine appellations, and complete rites in fact cannot be erased.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal notes: Though Xingzong and Ruizong never reigned, their titles and rites were complete and cannot be erased from record.

sentences.zh: 史者所以記事也，記事必核其名與實。

translations.literal: The historian exists to record events; recording events must verify name and reality.
translations.idiomatic: Historians record events, and events require names that match reality.

sentences.zh: 曰宗曰帝者，當時已定之名，名定而實著焉矣。

translations.literal: To say "lineage founder" or "emperor" is to use names fixed at the time; once the name is fixed, the reality is made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Titles of "founder" and "emperor" were fixed in their day; once named, the reality stands.

sentences.zh: 爰據《元史》裕宗、睿宗列傳之例，別為一卷如右，而各以后附焉。

translations.literal: Therefore, following the precedent of the biographies of Prince Yu and Prince Rui in the History of Yuan, a separate volume is set forth as above, with each consort appended afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Yuan History's biographies of Prince Yu and Prince Rui, this separate volume is arranged as above, with each consort treated in turn.
